ei.subject: 수능특강Light

fullPassage: For millions of years, hominids, our ancestors, had immense spaces at their disposal. According to a survey carried out by the United States Census Bureau, ten thousand years ago, just before the development of agriculture, the population of the planet numbered between 1 million and 10 million individuals. Until that time, vestiges were indeed found indicating that certain individuals were probably victims of murder, but no trace of war between groups has been found. According to the anthropologist Jonathan Haas: “Archaeologically, there is negligible evidence for any kind of warfare anywhere in the world before about 10,000 years ago.” That seems plausible if we think, along with Frans de Waal, that the first human societies lived in small scattered bands, far from each other, and had no reason to wage war. They were much more concerned with surviving and escaping predators prevalent at the time.

questions.passage: For millions of years, hominids, our ancestors, had (A)[immense / tiny] spaces at their disposal. According to a survey carried out by the United States Census Bureau, ten thousand years ago, just before the development of agriculture, the population of the planet numbered between 1 million and 10 million individuals. Until that time, vestiges were indeed found indicating that certain individuals were probably victims of murder, but no trace of war between groups has been found. According to the anthropologist Jonathan Haas: “Archaeologically, there is (B)[negligible / substantial] evidence for any kind of warfare anywhere in the world before about 10,000 years ago.” That seems plausible if we think, along with Frans de Waal, that the first human societies lived in small scattered bands, far from each other, and had no reason to wage war. They were much more concerned with surviving and escaping predators (C)[extinct / prevalent] at the time.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 거대한(immense), 무시할 만한(negligible), 만연한(prevalent)
det.analysis:
② immense — negligible — prevalent ←정답

① tiny — negligible — prevalent: (A)에 tiny(작은)는 부적절. 조상들이 '거대한(immense)' 공간을 이용했다는 맥락.

③ immense — substantial — prevalent: (B)에 substantial(상당한)은 부적절. 전쟁의 증거가 '무시할 만하다(negligible)'는 맥락.

④ immense — negligible — extinct: (C)에 extinct(멸종된)는 부적절. 당시 '만연한(prevalent)' 포식자라는 맥락.
det.tip: immense(거대한) ↔ tiny, negligible(무시할 만한) ↔ substantial, prevalent(만연한) ↔ extinct

questions.passage: For millions of years, hominids, our ancestors, had immense spaces at their disposal. According to a survey carried out by the United States Census Bureau, ten thousand years ago, just before the (A)[development / decline] of agriculture, the population of the planet numbered between 1 million and 10 million individuals. Until that time, vestiges were indeed found indicating that certain individuals were probably (B)[beneficiaries / victims] of murder, but no trace of war between groups has been found. According to the anthropologist Jonathan Haas: “Archaeologically, there is negligible evidence for any kind of warfare anywhere in the world before about 10,000 years ago.” That seems plausible if we think, along with Frans de Waal, that the first human societies lived in small (C)[concentrated / scattered] bands, far from each other, and had no reason to wage war. They were much more concerned with surviving and escaping predators prevalent at the time.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 발전(development), 희생자(victims), 흩어진(scattered)
det.analysis:
③ development — victims — scattered ←정답

① decline — victims — scattered: (A)에 decline(쇠퇴)은 부적절. 농업의 '발전(development)' 직전이라는 맥락.

② development — beneficiaries — scattered: (B)에 beneficiaries(수혜자)는 부적절. 살인의 '희생자(victims)'라는 맥락.

④ development — victims — concentrated: (C)에 concentrated(집중된)는 부적절. 서로 멀리 떨어진 '흩어진(scattered)' 무리라는 맥락.
det.tip: development(발전) ↔ decline, victims(희생자) ↔ beneficiaries, scattered(흩어진) ↔ concentrated

questions.passage: For millions of years, hominids, our ancestors, had immense spaces at their disposal. According to a survey (A)[made up / carried out] by the United States Census Bureau, ten thousand years ago, just before the development of agriculture, the population of the planet numbered between 1 million and 10 million individuals. Until that time, vestiges were indeed found indicating that certain individuals were probably victims of murder, but no trace of war between groups has been found. According to the anthropologist Jonathan Haas: “Archaeologically, there is negligible evidence for any kind of warfare anywhere in the world before about 10,000 years ago.” That seems (B)[absurd / plausible] if we think, along with Frans de Waal, that the first human societies lived in small scattered bands, far from each other, and had no reason to (C)[wage / avoid] war. They were much more concerned with surviving and escaping predators prevalent at the time.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 실시된(carried out), 그럴듯한(plausible), 벌이다(wage)
det.analysis:
① carried out — plausible — wage ←정답

② made up — plausible — wage: (A)에 made up(조작된)은 부적절. 조사가 '실시된(carried out)'이라는 맥락.

③ carried out — absurd — wage: (B)에 absurd(터무니없는)는 부적절. 흩어져 살았으므로 전쟁 없음이 '그럴듯하다(plausible)'는 맥락.

④ carried out — plausible — avoid: (C)에 avoid(피하다)는 부적절. 전쟁을 '벌일(wage)' 이유가 없었다는 맥락.
det.tip: carry out(실시하다) ↔ make up(조작하다), plausible(그럴듯한) ↔ absurd(터무니없는), wage war(전쟁을 벌이다)

They were much more concerned with ③<u>surviving</u> and ④<u>attracting</u> predators prevalent at the time.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ attracting(끌어들이는) → escaping(탈출하는). 포식자를 '피하는' 것이 맥락에 맞음.
det.analysis:
❌ ① agriculture: 농업. 적절.
❌ ② victims: 희생자. 적절.
❌ ③ surviving: 생존하는. 적절.
✅ ④ attracting → escaping: 원문은 escaping. 포식자를 '끌어들이는' 것은 반대.
det.tip: escaping(탈출하다) ↔ attracting(끌어들이다)

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ prevent(방지하다) → wage(벌이다). 전쟁을 '벌일' 이유가 없었다는 문맥.
det.analysis:
❌ ① disposal: 처분, 이용. 적절.
❌ ② vestiges: 흔적. 적절.
❌ ③ negligible: 무시할 만한. 적절.
✅ ④ prevent → wage: 원문은 wage. 전쟁을 '방지하다'가 아니라 '벌이다'.
det.tip: wage war(전쟁을 벌이다) ↔ prevent war(전쟁을 방지하다)

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ doubtful(의심스러운) → plausible(그럴듯한). 흩어져 살았으니 전쟁 없음이 '그럴듯하다'는 맥락.
det.analysis:
❌ ① immense: 거대한(huge). 넓은 공간이라는 맥락에 적절.
❌ ② indicating: 나타내는(showing). 흔적이 ~을 나타내다라는 맥락에 적절.
✅ ③ doubtful → plausible: 원문은 plausible(그럴듯한). 소규모 흩어진 사회였으므로 전쟁 없음이 '그럴듯하다'는 맥락에서 doubtful(의심스러운)은 반대.
❌ ④ predators: 포식자(천적). 적절.
det.tip: plausible(그럴듯한) ↔ doubtful(의심스러운)

questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 어떤 종류의 warfare(전쟁)에 대한 증거도 무시할 만하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① warfare: 전쟁. 전쟁 증거가 거의 없다는 인용문.
❌ ② agriculture: 농업. 빈칸 앞뒤 맥락과 무관.
❌ ③ murder: 살인. 앞 문장에서 이미 살인은 존재했다고 언급.
❌ ④ population: 인구. 빈칸 위치와 부합하지 않음.

questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 특정 개인이 살인의 희생자였음을 나타내는 vestiges(흔적)가 발견되었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ vestiges: 흔적, 자취. 고고학적 흔적이 발견되었다는 문맥.
❌ ① predators: 포식자. 빈칸 뒤 indicating과 어울리지 않음.
❌ ② weapons: 무기. 원문에 없는 단어이며 문맥도 흔적(vestiges)이 정확.
❌ ③ societies: 사회. 문맥상 '발견된(found)' 대상으로 부적합.

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>immense</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:

❌ ④ narrow: 좁은. 반대 개념.
det.tip: immense = enormous, vast, huge ↔ tiny, minimal

❌ ④ ancient: 고대의. 다른 의미.
det.tip: prevalent = widespread, common ↔ rare, uncommon

det.analysis:

questions.passage:

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 carried out이 (A)에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) carried out = 실시하다. (B) carried out = 운반하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 실시하다: (A)에서 조사를 '실시하다'라는 의미.
❌ ① 운반하다: (B)의 의미. 물건을 밖으로 옮기다.

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"traces or remains of something that once existed"

det.korean: 한때 존재했던 것의 흔적이나 잔재 → vestiges(흔적).
det.analysis:
✅ ① vestiges: 흔적(자취). 한때 존재했던 것의 남은 흔적이라는 영영풀이에 정확히 부합.

❌ ② predators: 포식자(천적). 다른 생물을 잡아먹는 동물로, 흔적이라는 뜻과 무관.

❌ ③ ancestors: 조상(선조). 앞 세대의 사람이라는 뜻으로 영영풀이와 불일치.

❌ ④ individuals: 개인(개체). 개별 사람이라는 뜻으로 영영풀이와 불일치.
det.tip: vestiges = traces, remains. 고고학적 맥락에서 자주 사용.

questions.passage: Until that time, vestiges were indeed found indicating that certain individuals were probably victims of murder, but no trace of war has been found. They were much more __________ (concern) with surviving and escaping predators.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어) (영어로)

det.korean: concern(동사/명사) → concerned(형용사). be concerned with = ~에 관심을 갖다.
det.analysis:
✅ concerned: 형용사. be concerned with ~에 관심을 갖다/걱정하다.
❌ concern: 원형. be 뒤에 형용사 필요.
❌ concerning: ~에 관하여(전치사). 문맥과 부합하지 않음.
det.tip: be concerned with = ~에 관심을 갖다, ~을 걱정하다

questions.passage: According to the anthropologist, there is __________ (neglect) evidence for any kind of warfare. That seems plausible if we think that the first human societies lived in small scattered bands.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어) (영어로)

det.korean: neglect(동사/명사) → negligible(형용사). 무시할 만한 증거.
det.analysis:
✅ negligible: 형용사. 무시할 만한. there is negligible evidence.
❌ neglected: 방치된. 문맥상 '무시할 만한'이 정확.
❌ neglectful: 태만한. 증거를 수식하기에 부적합.
det.tip: neglect → negligible(무시할 만한), neglected(방치된), negligent(태만한)

questions.passage: For millions of years, hominids, our ancestors, had immense spaces at their disposal. According to a survey carried out by the United States Census Bureau, ten thousand years ago, just before the development of agriculture, the population of the planet numbered between 1 million and 10 million individuals. Until that time, vestiges were indeed found indicating that certain individuals were probably __________, but no trace of war between groups has been found. According to the anthropologist Jonathan Haas: “Archaeologically, there is negligible evidence for any kind of warfare anywhere in the world before about 10,000 years ago.” That seems plausible if we think, along with Frans de Waal, that the first human societies lived in small scattered bands, far from each other, and had no reason to wage war. They were much more concerned with surviving and escaping predators prevalent at the time.
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 특정 개인이 살인의 victims of murder(살인의 희생자)였을 가능성이 있었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ victims of murder: 살인의 희생자. 개인적 살인은 있었지만 집단 전쟁은 없었다는 문맥.
❌ ① leaders of groups: 집단의 지도자. 무관.
❌ ② survivors of warfare: 전쟁의 생존자. 전쟁이 없었다는 맥락과 모순.
❌ ④ founders of agriculture: 농업의 창시자. 농업 발전 이전 시기라는 맥락과 부합하지 않음.
det.tip: victims of murder(살인의 희생자) — 개인적 폭력은 존재했으나 집단 전쟁은 없었음

questions.passage: For millions of years, hominids, our ancestors, had immense spaces at their disposal. According to a survey carried out by the United States Census Bureau, ten thousand years ago, just before the development of agriculture, the population of the planet numbered between 1 million and 10 million individuals. Until that time, vestiges were indeed found indicating that certain individuals were probably victims of murder, but no trace of war between groups has been found. According to the anthropologist Jonathan Haas: “Archaeologically, there is negligible evidence for any kind of warfare anywhere in the world before about 10,000 years ago.” That seems plausible if we think, along with Frans de Waal, that the first human societies lived in small scattered bands, far from each other, and had no reason to wage war. They were much more concerned with __________ prevalent at the time.
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 당시 만연한 surviving and escaping predators(생존하고 포식자를 피하는 것)에 관심이 더 많았다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① surviving and escaping predators: 생존하고 포식자를 피하는 것. 원문 그대로.
❌ ② developing agricultural techniques: 농업 기술 개발. 농업 이전 시기이므로 부적합.
❌ ③ waging wars against neighbors: 이웃과의 전쟁. 전쟁할 이유가 없었다는 맥락과 모순.
❌ ④ trading goods with other bands: 다른 집단과의 교역. 원문에 언급 없음.
det.tip: prevalent = 만연한. predators prevalent at the time = 당시 널리 존재하던 포식자들
